learning: Iteration 7 lowered yaw inertia and raised slalom progress (0.30 to 0.53), but line_loss_events rose to 1.3. Iteration 8 showed that narrowing the track to 0.09 m adds s-bend jitter (0.342) without fixing the slalom exit. Mass 0.5 kg tests whether the yaw-inertia lever continues to help or begins to overshoot.
notes: Runnable package: the iteration 7 design with mass reduced from 0.6 to 0.5 kg and wheel_track restored to 0.10 m (the iteration 8 value of 0.09 m is dropped). The controller is unchanged from iteration 7, so mass is the only variable under test.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 7 (mass 0.6 kg, body 0.12 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, kp 3.6, kd 0.9) is the best design at 707.2. Its oval finished 20/20 at 1.79 s, its s-bend 20/20 with steering_oscillation 0.311, and its slalom 0/20 with progress up to 0.53 and line_loss_events 1.3. Iteration 8 (wheel_track 0.09 m) lost an s-bend finish and pushed jitter to 0.342, while slalom progress fell to 0.42. Narrowing the track is therefore ruled out, and the design returns to wheel_track 0.10 m. Lower yaw inertia is the only lever that has moved slalom progress, so this step tests a further reduction by setting mass to 0.5 kg with body_length 0.12 m (about 17 percent lower yaw inertia). Sensing (seven 12 mm sensors at 0.012 m pitch, span plus or minus 0.036 m, lead 0.06 m), wheel_radius 0.03 m and body_width 0.12 m are unchanged. The controller is kept exactly as in iteration 7 (kp 3.6, kd 0.9, ki 0, weights -2 to +2, base_speed 1.6, last_direction), so the race isolates mass. Mass 0.5 is inside the 0.4 to 1.5 kg range. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.53 with line_loss_events moving toward 1.0, the oval at 20/20, and the s-bend at 19/20 or better with steering_oscillation under 0.35. Risk: the faster-turning robot overshoots at direction changes. If the s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.35 or the score falls below 707, the fallback is the iteration 7 design (mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.10 m).
